title: BACK 2 THE GYM STREAM (Program reviews & Answering training questions)
summary: A four-hour monthly hypertrophy Q&A stream where NH answers chat and Ko-fi questions and reviews viewer programs live. His recurring criticisms are redundant exercises, junk volume, too much triceps work, and templates followed blindly. He praises minimalist programs that pair a press with a pull and add isolation, and he defends low-volume, high-intensity training, lean slow bulks and pullovers.
claims: A good personal trainer should have the abilities they claim to build in you, or a track record of clients who started out struggling and got there
A good PT prepares each session in advance, stays off the phone, corrects your form, is encouraging, and teaches you to stop needing them
Machine pullovers are easier to set up than dumbbell pullovers, may recruit the abs more and suit rest-pause better, and are the closest substitute; the cable version is far removed
Pullovers should be in every program; they fit any push or upper body day
The tibialis cannot get monstrously big because the bone it sits on limits it, but it can grow enough to be visible from the side
Olympic lifts are terrible for hypertrophy because they are highly technical and depend on balance; power cleans and snatch-grip variants are more usable
He dislikes cross-arm front squats as a safety matter because one shoulder must sit higher than the other
With narrow clavicles you can still build shoulder width with deltoid mass; he has about a 3-head shoulder-to-head ratio, while 4 heads is the heroic ratio and comes only from genetics
Lengthened partials can work since the lengthened portion drives growth, but he finds them awkward, prefers clean sets with a clear start and end, and gets more from rest-pause
Do forearm curls and extensions even if you already do hammer curls and carries: 15 reps cost almost no fatigue, superset with anything, and give free forearm volume
The fix for a pencil neck is simply to train the neck directly
For one erector bigger than the other, do single-leg hyperextensions or single-leg RDLs, since fighting hip rotation loads one side more
StrongLifts 5x5 builds mass and strength in beginners but is imbalanced and lacks isolation; old programs like it should be dropped for free programs by natural bodybuilders on Boostcamp
Machine rows and Meadows rows are both horizontal pulls but serve different purposes; Meadows rows done properly hit the rear delts much more
Front squats are limited by holding the rack position; for front-loaded quad work he prefers hack squats or belt squats, and he finds the strap trick awkward
He has never tried breathing squats for ribcage expansion, but Steve Reeves credited them, so they are worth testing
Women should train more lower body than men because they have more capacity there; bench press is not necessary for them and flyes can do the job
Women do like muscle, but chest, shoulders, arms, abs and glutes, not the mass-monster look
Novices do not need straps at first; put them on as soon as grip becomes the limiting factor
Put pullovers on pressing days at the end of the session. A good layout is heavy horizontal press with forearms, then vertical press with a pull, then pullover with biceps isolation
To handle the burn, lower the rep range (for example from 10-15 to 8-12) because higher reps build up more lactic acid, and push through the pain since it does not injure you
To build tolerance to the burn, use rest-pause: stop when it hurts, wait 10 seconds, and get 3-4 more reps
Nucleus overload works whether you are bulking or cutting
For elbow pain on JM presses, vary grip width (wide, medium, narrow) as Todd Hutchings advises; if a lift still hurts, drop it for a while and come back
Dips once hurt him; he took time away and now does them with four extra plates, so tendons can adapt
Supersetting overhead press with lateral raises is a mistake because both hit the delts and the isolation suffers; that day also had too many shoulder exercises
Three training days a week is a perfectly fine frequency
Weighted pull-ups belong at low reps; 5-8 is the upper limit, and 8-12 is overkill that stops you loading them heavily
Hanging knee raises must eventually be weighted, and repeating only one ab movement can limit ab growth, so vary it
Rather than repeating lateral raises on several days, rotate in upright rows or Y-raises to cut overuse injuries and keep performance progressing
Ring dips followed by ring push-ups on the same day are redundant; rotate the two instead
Lots of pressing does not give the triceps what they need when you are chest- or shoulder-dominant; that is why triceps isolation exists
He respects strength athletes; elite Olympic lifters may train a full year to add 2 kg to their snatch
Neck training once or twice a week already gives great results; more than 3-4 sessions a week is pointless and risks overuse injury. Forearms are the only thing to spam
Nobody can make you train; find the reason in yourself, because training improves mental health, longevity and strength
You can stay on a program like his Ultimate Hypertrophy program indefinitely as long as you keep progressing and enjoy it

For a home gym with no space for a rack, get a combined dip/pull-up station and compact squat stands. Avoid adjustable dumbbells because the extra plates get expensive; buy used dumbbells from closing gyms or private sellers
If dips cause sternum pain, stop doing them and let it settle instead of training through it
Bad posture is real; it looks bad and is linked to back pain. Train traps (face pulls), abs and lower back, use a lumbar pillow and a straight-backed chair, and hold posture deliberately
Behind-the-neck presses force an exaggerated upright posture and so reinforce good posture
Vascularity comes mostly from training and being lean; garlic is the only food he would credit
Once you can do 10-15 clean bodyweight dips or pull-ups, add weight, even 5 lb, because bodyweight reps stall and stop driving hypertrophy
Two hard sets of heavy squats are enough if two more quad sets follow later in the session
Abs left to the end of the session usually get sandbagged or skipped; move them earlier, for example between two presses
If lying leg curls are the only hamstring movement, a quad/hamstring imbalance can develop; include heavy posterior-chain work
Giant sets of three isolation movements (triceps, biceps, delts) work because isolation is not systemically fatiguing; the cardio limit goes away with practice
Lying triceps extensions after dips and Smith JM presses will perform poorly; that much triceps work in a row is questionable
To manage hunger on a cut, eat low-calorie filling foods, eat protein, and save calories for the evening so you do not go to bed hungry. He has only ever done one unhealthy crash cut
Rings trade stability for range of motion on dips; he prefers a dip bar because it was made for dips
He now recomps in summer, when it is too hot to eat much, and bulks very slowly in winter
Online natural bodybuilding competitions lose money; Nick Strength and Power ran one and never repeated it
Warm up only for the first exercise of a movement line; follow-ups like flyes after heavy bench need at most one warm-up set
Calf raises on a seated leg press are good because only the calves move the weight
Novices should isolate their forearms from day one so they never become an intermediate with stick forearms
The biggest regulars at a gym are the most supportive; novices should not be afraid of them
He has 6-inch wrists and small hands but big arms, proof that small joints do not block arm size
Bulking up to around 20% body fat is a bad idea for most people; you just get fat
A rep drop across sets (7, 7, 7 then 8, 7, 7) is no cause for worry as long as the top set progresses
Even demanding studies like medicine leave room for lifting; 45 minutes 2-3 times a week at home helped his own mental health in grad school
His current split is upper/lower 5 days a week: two lower days and three upper days, two torso-focused and one arm-focused
Most 135 lb curl claims are cheated with elbows, hips or knees; strict incline curls with about 25 lb hit the biceps, and isolation demands humility
Physique archetypes he names: spider mode, otter mode, barbarian mode, hippo mode, frog mode (big legs, tiny upper body) and lobster mode (huge limbs, no torso)
Smith machine squats are S-tier with feet forward and hips forward because the machine replaces the hip hinge; copying free-weight technique on the Smith is bad, and novices should learn free squats
When bulking, most of his calories come from carbs
If pullovers hit the triceps and not the lats, it is likely long arms; bend the elbows more or use an EZ bar
Trap bar deadlifts are useless for quads: little knee bend and no loaded eccentric
Dips and pull-ups are underrated for hypertrophy
If he cut he would count calories, because eating by appetite fails
Do not do RDLs right after heavy deadlifts taken to failure; rotate them on different weeks
Weighted chin-ups are the riskiest pull-up because a supinated grip overextended under load can tear the biceps tendon, which has happened to elite athletes
Dips twice a week, especially an unweighted session that does not progress, invite overuse injuries; replace one with a similar non-dip movement
Cutting excess volume often improves performance, speeds up progressive overload and helps recovery; he sits closer to HIT than to 18-20 sets per muscle
Light submaximal calisthenics next to lifting is fine; training for skills like a muscle-up or planche costs real recovery
Manual laborers should train intensely but as rarely and with as little volume as possible, since work already gives them volume
After hurting your back on barbell RDLs, build up hyperextensions and dumbbell RDLs first; dumbbells make it easier to push the hips back
Full body training makes it hard to fit much isolation, and 18 exercises per session likely contains junk volume
Obliques are underrated and will not make your waist blocky; train them with side bends on a hyperextension bench, Russian twists and suitcase deadlifts
It is normal not to look like you lift after one year; it took him 3-4 years
Ten exercises on an upper day is not too many given how many muscles need covering; his own gym upper days have 6 exercises, done 3 times a week
The idea that exercise ages you is bogus; exercise is the fountain of youth, and the sedentary people he knows break down first
A 190 cm, 81 kg lifter at about 15% body fat should slow bulk rather than cut
Training back on consecutive days works if you split the parts, but different back exercises can share movement patterns
When submitting a program for review, mention your other sports; martial artists need less lifting volume, and trap bar deadlifts suit them because they keep the torso upright
Preacher curls need a minimum of 6 reps; 6-12 gives a cushion for a risky lift
Lifting three times a week on top of three martial arts sessions with long exercise lists means chasing two rabbits; cut sets and exercises
Dumbbell-only training is limited for legs and for isolating muscles like the triceps; cables are a big upgrade
Full body sessions on back-to-back days are a bad idea; full body suits training 2-3 times a week with rest between
He no longer believes in supersetting triceps extensions with presses; that pairing appears only in his old programs
He can take his lats to failure one day and do RDLs the next without lower performance, so he doubts the idea that the previous day's training hurts the next
Deadlifts do not replace rows; the deadlift is a lower body movement, not an upper back movement
He does triceps pushdowns with cuffs to avoid the balance problem of leaning over the handle
Squats for 5x5 are not a great rep scheme for hypertrophy
Too much triceps work spread across the week keeps them fatigued and stops them growing
If you lose your love for lifting, try a new sport and do only the movements you enjoy
If you are injured for weeks during a bulk, stop bulking and do a mini cut, since you cannot train
If you are progressing without a surplus, there is no point adding calories
A 200 kcal surplus is enough for a bulk
He never trains fasted because it hurts his performance, and he eats as soon as he wakes up
When combining kickboxing twice a week with lifting, lift the day after kickboxing
Dropping to low reps to break a bench plateau is fine for hypertrophy trainees, just not too often
The deadlift is poor for hypertrophy: no real eccentric, heavy loads that limit you to 3-5 reps, and fatigue that drags down the rest of the session. The RDL has a better stimulus-to-fatigue ratio
Gaining 10 lb a year is too much for an advanced 200 lb lifter; 5 lb a year is enough on a bulk
Natural bodybuilders should stay presentable year-round at 12-15% body fat as silver-era bodybuilders did; extreme leanness is for social media
Skip fake tans; get about 20 minutes of sun a day in moderation for skin tone and health, carefully if you burn easily
His weekly volume: chest 6 sets, triceps 9, biceps 9, upper back 10-12, shoulders 9-12; he is low on the volume spectrum and believes in hard sets
He deliberately does 6 chest sets and 9-12 shoulder sets a week so the shoulders catch up; his chest still grows on 6 sets
The two-set method means short compact days with minimal volume and high intensity; adding extra exercises defeats its purpose
Do not be a slave to a program template; fill a torso day with useful arm work, not redundant exercises
A dedicated arm day often becomes junk isolation volume to make up for neglecting arms elsewhere
Recovery is just rest: eat, sleep as much as you can, be lazy; you do not need active recovery
Do overhead pressing before lateral raises because it is the compound
Shoulder-dominant lifters can skip vertical presses entirely; a natural with huge shoulders at his gym does
Muscle mass protects you in old age; long-time trainees can have about five times more leg muscle than untrained people, and studies linking muscle to shorter life are inconclusive
His strongest muscles visually are the biceps and abs, his weakest the triceps and shoulders
Rear delts benefit from higher reps
A lifter with huge legs who wants upper body to catch up must cut leg volume; dominant body parts will not shrink and may keep growing
Supersetting non-taxing isolation movements saves a lot of time
A minimalist upper day (one vertical press, one vertical pull, one incline press, a pullover, two arm isolations, abs) is the base of what you need; add only when it stops working
Six sets of sit-ups in a session is too much; three is right
When you max out the gym's dumbbells on rows, slow the tempo
Cutting 20% of leg volume on dominant legs will make no difference to gains
HIT beats German Volume Training because it leaves room to add volume, while GVT can only regress
Compound-heavy strength templates with isolation tacked on create imbalanced physiques, like lots of pressing and only 3 sets of curls, which leads to small arms
Wide backup-set ranges such as 1-8 total sets of bench are too hard to control; 3-6 sets is already a big range
Doing deadlifts twice a week is redundant; swap one for another hip hinge
Gaining 14 kg in 4 years is good; do not compare your rate with others or you risk overbulking
For MMA fighters, heavy deadlifts twice a week waste energy; single-leg work, Zercher deadlifts or light Jefferson curls carry over better
He has scoliosis and deadlifts heavy without issues
Novices do not need five sessions a week, grip variations on rows, or 4 sets of 6-12 deadlifts; they overdo compounds
When forced to choose between sleep and training, do a minimal 20-minute session
Being much stronger on seated overhead press than on bench is not a problem unless the shoulders visually overpower the chest
To stop fatiguing before failure in supersets, build work capacity and eat before training
He is against stimulant pre-workouts because needing to be wired to train builds an unhealthy relationship with lifting
Bulgarian split squats beat hip thrusts when time is short; hip thrusts need huge loads
Preacher hammer curls are excellent; he now does them standing beside the bench for a huge stretch, and they are easy on the tendons
Bench press shifting likely comes from uneven shoulders; stop touch-and-go and use paused reps
Pronation curls are vastly superior to Zottman curls
Leg curls with a dumbbell are not recommended because the strength curve is all over the place
Mike Mentzer was right to focus on intensity but went too far
Flattering lighting and photoshopped thumbnails are dishonest; he saw two 160 lb guys staging a gym photoshoot who looked small in person
In a commercial gym, superset equipment that sits close together and accept the gamble when it is far apart
ChatGPT gives better fitness advice than many fitness YouTubers but only regurgitates what is online
